comments: Smoke test: cross-compilation target flag parsing and codegen dispatch.
The Mach-O (write_macho_x86 / write_macho_arm64) and PE/COFF (write_pe) backends
were implemented but previously undocumented as "not yet wired".  They are in fact
dispatched by the codegen driver in main() based on TARGET_OS / TARGET_ARCH:
--target x86_64-linux   → TARGET_OS=0, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_elf()       (default)
--target aarch64-linux  → TARGET_OS=0, TARGET_ARCH=1 → write_elf_arm64()
--target x86_64-macos   → TARGET_OS=2, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_macho_x86()
--target aarch64-macos  → TARGET_OS=2, TARGET_ARCH=1 → write_macho_arm64()
--target x86_64-windows → TARGET_OS=3, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_pe()
This file is a minimal Sounio program that compiles and runs correctly on Linux
(the host platform).  The cross-compilation targets require running the produced
binary on the corresponding OS; the compiler itself will emit a valid Mach-O or
PE/COFF file when invoked with the appropriate --target flag.
To manually verify cross-compile flag acceptance:
$SOUC compile tests/run-pass/cross_compile_flag.sio -o /tmp/out.macho --target x86_64-macos
$SOUC compile tests/run-pass/cross_compile_flag.sio -o /tmp/out.pe    --target x86_64-windows
Both commands should succeed with exit code 0 and emit the respective binary format.

comments: `outer.boxed.field` — a field access whose BASE is a field of type Box<T>.
expr_receiver_struct_type_ref recursed to Outer correctly and then answered
with the literal "Box", the declared type of `boxed`. A non-empty name reads
as TYPED, so field_idx_from_name("Box", "b") found no such layout and fell
through to the cross-struct FIRST-MATCH scan. `b` is index 1 in Inner and
index 2 in Decoy, so the read landed on Inner's index 2 and returned 30.
Silent wrong value, not a crash — which is why it survived: Decoy is declared
first so it wins the scan, exactly as HlirModule wins over IrModule for
`fn_count` in find_or_add_fn_id (gen2 SIGSEGV, module 7).
`direct` is the control: the same field read through a plain reference, which
never used the by-name path and was always right. If a fix breaks THAT, it
broke Box deref rather than field typing.

description: a call's arguments must survive an arena round trip (#1649 rc=12 regression)
comments: This is the shape that broke the whole SoA arena branch. `ir_arena_load`
cannot rebuild a call's argument list -- that needs Alloc, and forcing Alloc
onto ~431 call sites is what desynchronised the checker -- so a loaded
instruction arrives with arg_count > 0 and no list. `ir_arena_store` used to
walk that empty list and write IR_INVALID_REG once per argument, and codegen
then reported the function unsupported:
NV2_IR missing_call_arg fn=main i=1 arg_index=0 arg_count=1
Error: Failed to write native binary ... rc=12
A call with NO arguments was unaffected, so single-function programs kept
compiling and the branch's self-compile stayed green throughout -- it is built
by the seed, which does not carry the defect. One argument is enough to catch
the regression; keep it that way.

description: Finding 11 (issue #2084): u64 >>, /, % must use unsigned semantics. At the dispatch point these three operations had a single BinaryOp variant each (OpShr, OpDiv, OpRem) that the lowering always emitted as the signed
comments: Finding 11 (issue #2084): u64 >>, /, % must use unsigned semantics.
At the dispatch point these three operations had a single BinaryOp variant
each (OpShr, OpDiv, OpRem) that the lowering always emitted as the signed
x86 instruction (sar rax,cl / idiv rcx). For a u64 value with bit 63 set
that gives mathematically wrong answers with no error:
- 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 >> 1 expected 0x7FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF (unsigned)
sar gives                    0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF (sign-extends)
- 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 /  2 expected 0x7FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF (unsigned)
idiv gives                            0 (treats as -1, truncate-toward-zero)
- 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 %  2 expected                    1 (unsigned)
idiv gives                           -1 (i.e. the input unchanged)
Bit-63-set is the boundary: a value with bit 62 set already shifts correctly
because the sign bit stays 0 under sar. + - * & | ^ << == != are unaffected.
This fixture MUST fail on unfixed main (where the lowering always emits the
signed instruction) and PASS once BinaryOp carries OpUDiv/OpURem/OpUShr and
the lowering routes them to div r/m64 / shr rax,cl.
